claims.text: High-temperature plastic strain and toughness in refractory plasma-facing materials are controlled by the degree of lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion modifies dislocation core structures.
Severe lattice distortion shifts deformation from conventional screw-dominated motion to a wavy, edge-dominated slip mode.
The edge-dominated mode reduces dislocation pile-ups and promotes homogeneous, ductile plastic flow at high temperature.
A conventional low-complexity BCC refractory alloy with minor lattice distortion can serve as the baseline.
Adding multiple principal elements to form a high-entropy alloy induces severe lattice distortion.
Elevated-temperature mechanical testing can be conducted up to approximately 900°C at a strain rate of approximately 1×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹.
Testing at 900°C and approximately 1×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ simulates fusion plasma-facing operational conditions.
Severe lattice distortion creates non-planar edge dislocation cores with reduced activation barriers for motion.
Reduced activation barriers decrease dislocation pile-up and make plastic deformation more uniform.
More uniform plastic deformation enhances high-temperature toughness.
The lattice-distorted HEA will show a smaller temperature-induced decrease in yield strength than the conventional baseline.
The lattice-distorted HEA will exhibit greater high-temperature plastic strain than the conventional baseline.
The lattice-distorted HEA will exhibit greater high-temperature toughness than the conventional baseline.
Microscopy will reveal predominantly modified, wavy edge dislocation cores in the HEA.
Conventional BCC refractory alloys are dominated by screw dislocations with higher barriers at high temperature.
The proposed hypothesis applies to refractory alloys that retain a stable BCC or similar structure up to approximately 900°C.
The hypothesis may not apply when crystal structure, grain-size effects, or secondary phases dominate plasticity.
The cited evidence supports the proposition that lattice distortion alters dislocation behavior.
